name: Boogie Down Productions
hook: Answered a record they heard as writing the Bronx out of hip-hop's own origin story, and won the argument so completely it ended the other side's career momentum.

blurb.age7: A Bronx rapper and his DJ heard a song from another neighbourhood that sounded like it was taking credit for starting rap, so they wrote an angry song back, and most people think they won.
blurb.age13: KRS-One and DJ Scott La Rock formed Boogie Down Productions in the South Bronx. After hearing MC Shan's 'The Bridge' as a claim that hip-hop began in Queensbridge, they answered first with 'South Bronx' and then 'The Bridge Is Over' (both 1986-87), asserting the Bronx's originator status and starting the Bridge Wars. Scott La Rock was shot and killed in the Bronx in August 1987, months after their debut album 'Criminal Minded' came out; KRS-One continued the group afterward and later went on to a long solo career.
blurb.adult: Boogie Down Productions' side of the Bridge Wars is widely treated as hip-hop's first well-documented example of a diss record settling an argument decisively in the court of public opinion; 'The Bridge Is Over' is still commonly ranked among the genre's most effective answer records. Scott La Rock's murder, while attempting to mediate an unrelated dispute involving a group member, cut short a production partnership only a year old and shaped KRS-One's subsequent turn toward explicitly political material.

signatureTracks.title: South Bronx
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The first answer record in the Bridge Wars, asserting the Bronx's claim as hip-hop's birthplace against 'The Bridge'.

signatureTracks.title: The Bridge Is Over
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The Bridge Wars' decisive record: same subject and format as MC Shan's original, turned into a direct, widely cited takedown.
